rule.summary: one REV ticket per session from the FIXED FTN Month 9 kernel at 9bed235, evaluated on bar-derived DayContext (BID chart, ASK series attached for spread_measured) at every 15m close inside the killzone; direction from the raid; stop beyond the raid's own extreme plus the instrument buffer; minimum stop distance enforced
rule.kernel: ftn.research.kernel_log.session_ticket_log(..., book=None) with config interpretation_triggers all false (ftn/config.yaml as pinned) -> ftn.os.candidates.evaluate_candidates; first selection in the session is the ticket. DayContext from ftn.research.daycontext.History(bid, days, ask=ask, calendar=True)
rule.sessions: London killzone 02:00-05:00 and NY AM killzone 07:00-10:00, America/New_York wall clock; kernel evaluated at each 15m close from start+15m to end inclusive, using only bars up to that close
rule.direction: REV: high raided -> bearish (short), low raided -> bullish (long); both or neither raided -> no ticket (ftn.models.rev.rev_direction)
rule.entry: close of the 15m bar on which the kernel first selects REV
rule.stop: bearish: raid_extreme_high + buffer, buffer = max(1 pt, max(spread_measured, assumed spread) + stop slippage) (US100 assumed spread 1.55 + 0.50 -> >= 2.05 pt; US500 0.72 + 0.25 -> >= 1.0 pt); bullish: raid_extreme_low - max(1 pt, stop slippage) (= 1 pt for both). raid_extreme as in H015b (15m bars from the raid bar to the entry bar). spread_measured = ASK close - BID close at the signal time. ftn.os.instruments.rev_stop_buffer; ftn.os.mint_draft REV _stop
rule.target_and_exit: fixed 2R from the signal entry (BID close); else time exit at the last 1m close before 16:00 NY; stop first on an ambiguous bar. Fills per costs.binding (correct side)
rule.tradeable: every research-draft gate passes except allowlist and the I0 contract gate (ftn.research.kernel_log.tradeable); D18 direction gate, stop-side risk gate and the min-stop gate active; the risk gate sees a FLAT book (kernel_log.FLAT_BOOK) in the binding stream
rule.context_history: the kernel needs >= 22 prior sessions of 1m bars as context; context bars may come from before the counting window (never counted)
rule.min_stop: risk gate blocks a ticket whose |entry - stop| < min_risk = 4 x (assumed spread + 2 x stop/market slippage): US100 10.2 pt, US500 4.88 pt (risk:stop_below_min_risk). A blocked ticket is NOT a trade and is not counted (ex-ante rule, not outcome-dependent); blocks are counted and reported
rule.month8_units: Month-8 measurements in instrument units (1 pip = 1 index point); index CBDR/Asian thresholds = ICT FX thresholds x (median daily range / EURUSD median daily range): US100 x6.743 (CBDR ideal < 269.7, wide >= 337.2), US500 x1.218
rule.calendar: FOMC/CPI/NFP schedule (ftn/src/ftn/research/data/us_macro_events.csv, pinned) is attached as context. The Month 9 kernel does not read it (ftn.research.events docstring); checked at 9bed235 on the burned tape (2026-10-04): calendar on vs --no-calendar gives identical trades (date, killzone, direction, entry, stop, R; US100 146/146, US500 112/112), only the fingerprint, calendar and m8_london_gate log columns differ; the harness must repeat this assertion. The pinned file has CPI/NFP only to 2026-12 and FOMC to 2027-12; it is never extended in the binding run (FTN_EVENTS_CSV override forbidden); an extended DATA-certified calendar may be used only in a separate co-report run
rule.entry_minute: BINDING (CASSANDRA F1): the kernel's entry price is BID.close_at(t) and spread_measured is ASK.close_at(t) - entry, both 'last bar strictly before t' (ftn.research.bars.Series.close_at), and simulate_both fills the entry at ask.c[ask.idx(t)-1] / bid.c[bid.idx(t)-1]. A ticket therefore counts only if a BID bar AND an ASK bar exist with timestamp EXACTLY t - 1 minute; otherwise the row status is feed_gap_entry (not counted, reported with counts). Evaluated for every ticket before any outcome is computed. Burned example: 2026-03-23 US100 ny_am, BID and ASK missing 07:06-07:17 NY, the 07:15 long entered at the stale 07:05 close: phantom +1.984R
rule.no_r_tickets: a tradeable ticket whose binding outcome is R=None (no_entry_bar, no_bars, invalid_stop) is NOT counted; status no_r_ticket, reported with counts by reason

data_source.feed: canonical Dukascopy datafeed CFD 1m bars, BID (BID_candles_min_1.bi5) AND ASK (ASK_candles_min_1.bi5) day files for USATECHIDXUSD and USA500IDXUSD, downloaded after each session closes; context bars included. BID drives the kernel chart and levels; ASK drives the correct-side fills and spread_measured. Both sides are BINDING
data_source.both_sides_required: a session counts per instrument only if BID and ASK day files are FINAL and complete for UTC days d-1 and d, BID and ASK each pass the killzone min-bar filter (>= 171/180) and the exit-bar rule; a ticket additionally needs the t-1m BID and ASK bars (rule.entry_minute)
data_source.why_not_capitalcom: the kernel needs >= 22 sessions of 1m context and full RTH coverage for the trading-day filter; TradingView CAPITALCOM serves ~5 sessions (research/forward/README.md open issue 2). The rule is fully mechanical and causal on bars, so computing a session after it closes gives the same ticket as computing it live; no live alert is required
data_source.certification: DATA must certify the forward BID+ASK download pipeline (H015b checklist C1-C13 incl. C3/C13 ASK items, adapted to H016b, with the C3/C13 ASK items covering the binding ASK use (CASSANDRA F8)) and write DATA_CERTIFIED.json with the H016b harness digest before any R is shown
data_source.raw_bars_required: every counted session persists the raw BID and ASK 1m day files consumed (context + session) with sha256 per file; the log row carries both session hashes and a context manifest hash; no fallback feeds, no filled gaps. A row without raw bars does not count
data_source.feed_disclosure: every H016b report states the feed is Dukascopy CFD BID+ASK, unlike H013/H014 (TradingView CAPITALCOM) and unlike H015b's binding BID-only stream
data_source.fallback_detail: no HistData, marketdata-merged, TradingView, broker or synthetic ASK (BID + assumed spread) substitute, ever; a missing side = session not counted (status feed_gap_bid / feed_gap_ask)
data_source.ask_minutes_after_entry: after the entry, BID minutes without an ASK print are skipped by simulate_both's exit loop (no exit is filled on a minute without a print on the exit side); their count is logged per trade (ask_gap_minutes). The ENTRY and spread_measured are never stale: rule.entry_minute. (Corrects H016 data_source.both_sides_required)
data_source.feed_suspension: a schema failure (feed_suspended) or more than 10 consecutive expected trading days whose rows are all feed_gap suspends counting from the first such date until DATA writes FEED_RESUMED.json; the feed is never switched (CASSANDRA F12b)

costs.binding: correct-side fills, ftn.research.outcomes.simulate_both(slip_mult=1.0): long enters on ASK close + market slip, stopped when BID low <= stop (fill min(stop, BID open) - stop slip), target when BID high > target (fill target - limit slip); short enters on BID close - market slip, stopped when ASK high >= stop (fill max(stop, ASK open) + stop slip), target when ASK low < target (fill target + limit slip). R = (exit fill - entry fill) / planned risk |signal entry - stop|
costs.source: DATA ruling 3 (/workspace/marketdata README), encoded in ftn/src/ftn/os/instruments.py (pinned)
co_reports: flat cost 0.8 / 0.5 pt per side (ftn.research.outcomes.simulate; H013/H014/H015b convention) - co-report ONLY (CASSANDRA)
measured spread at the signal (monthly median / p90 per instrument and killzone)

counting_rules.first_eligible_session: the first killzone session that starts after the prereg-H016b tag is pushed AND (rule 5) whose row is computed after the H016b harness registration commit: London 2026-10-05 02:00 NY (08:00 SAST) if both precede it
counting_rules.forward_only_why: forward-only: the fixes were chosen after seeing the burned window, and 2026-09-26..2026-10-04 plus DATA's certified-untouched ranges must stay unread before registration. Forward-only means no one, human or agent, can have seen the outcome
counting_rules.excluded: every session dated before 2026-10-05 is never counted (it may be used only as kernel context history)
counting_rules.trading_day_filter: weekday with >= 300 1m bars in 09:30-15:59 NY on the feed (ftn.research.bars.trading_days), per instrument (BID)
counting_rules.min_bar_filter: a session counts per instrument only if >= 171 of 180 1m bars are present in its killzone on BID and on ASK, and the exit-bar rule holds

holidays_excluded.maintenance: DATA extends the list from the NYSE published calendar (holiday_source) before each new year's first session

counting_rules.backfill: all rows are computed after the session closes from saved raw bars; rows are flagged with compute time; recomputation must reproduce the stored row exactly
counting_rules.timezone: America/New_York wall clock for all rule times
counting_rules.exit_bar_rule: BINDING (CASSANDRA F4; = H015b v2 appendix A4): at least one BID bar AND at least one ASK bar in [15:45, 16:00) NY on date d, evaluated for EVERY session of the day before the trade/no_trade branch, so session validity never depends on the entry. Failing it -> short_session (not counted). A gap > 5 min between entry and 16:00 on either side is a NON-binding gap_flag
counting_rules.computed_after_harness_registration: BINDING (CASSANDRA F6): a row counts only if its compute time is later than the commit time on origin of the first H016b harness registration note (status REGISTERED); no forward bar file (dated >= 2026-09-26) is downloaded or opened by anyone before that commit; the downloader is part of the registered harness; the harness must reproduce the burned H016 trades bit-for-bit at its digest before its first forward pull
counting_rules.holiday_source: the binding holiday/early-close source is the NYSE published holiday calendar (nyse.com markets/hours-calendars); the listed dates are as registered; dates not yet listed are added by DATA from that source before each year's first session; a discrepancy with the NYSE publication is resolved in favour of the NYSE publication (CASSANDRA F12e)
counting_rules.calendar_identity: per forward session the harness asserts the ticket (date, killzone, side, entry_time, entry, stop) is identical with the macro calendar on and off (fingerprint excluded); a difference refuses the row (CASSANDRA F12c)

primary_metric: pooled mean R per ticket after correct-side costs, over ALL eligible tickets (flat-book gating; entry-minute, exit-bar and min-bar rules applied)

binding_metric_choice.decision: per-ticket R on all eligible tickets (risk gate sees a flat book) is BINDING; the running paper book is a required co-report
binding_metric_choice.running_book_spec: ftn.research.book.RunningBook: start equity 100, each taken trade risks 0.5% of current equity (max_trade_risk_pct), 2% daily loss cap (realised loss today vs start-of-day equity, NY date), 5% drawdown cap from the high-water mark; drawdown_reset next_calendar_month (after the 5% cap blocks a ticket, halted for the rest of that calendar month, HWM reset to current equity at the first ticket of a later month); P&L realised at exit time; the gate sees realised trades only
justification: the book's freezes depend on earlier outcomes, so the running-book sample is an outcome-dependent selection of tickets: it is not the rule's ticket population and breaks the exchangeable-cluster assumption of the bootstrap

freezes shrink N and power: on the burned window the running book dropped 6/146 US100 and 12/112 US500 trades (max_drawdown_cap) - about 7% of trades, more under a true-zero edge, which would lengthen the test or lower power

the hypothesis is about the rule's per-ticket edge; the caps are a risk-management layer for MINT that must be judged on the same tickets, so the running book is co-reported (mean R, total R, equity, max DD %, freeze count, tickets lost) and never changes a verdict
the min-stop block is an ex-ante part of the rule (not outcome-dependent) and therefore applies in the binding stream

statistical_test.hypothesis: one-sided: pooled mean R per ticket after correct-side costs > 0
statistical_test.binding_bound: session-cluster percentile bootstrap. Clusters = (date, killzone) over counted trades pooled across US100 and US500, in canonical order (date, london before ny_am). rng = random.Random(20261004); 10,000 resamples; each resample draws k clusters with rng.randrange(k) (k = number of clusters) and computes sum(R)/count(trades). Sorted values v[0..9999]. Binding one-sided 95% lower bound = v[int(0.05*10000)] = v[500] (the 5th percentile; alpha = 0.05 one-sided). PASS needs v[500] > 0
statistical_test.p_value_for_family_rule: one-sided p = (#{v <= 0} + 1) / 10,001 from the same cluster bootstrap
statistical_test.percentile_warning: ftn.research.stats.boot_ci(alpha=0.05) returns v[250], the 2.5th percentile (a two-sided 95% / one-sided 97.5% bound). It is NOT the binding call. The harness implements the cluster bootstrap itself and a unit test asserts the binding index is 500
statistical_test.co_report_trade_level: trade-level percentile bootstrap, same seed and resample count, one-sided 95% lower bound = ftn.research.stats.boot_ci(R, alpha=0.10)[0] (non-binding)
statistical_test.multiplicity: H016b has one primary hypothesis. Promotion is governed by family_rule; FTN-H001..H013 conditioning reads are exploratory only
statistical_test.binding_call: harness-implemented session-cluster percentile bootstrap (NOT ftn.research.stats.boot_ci): rng = random.Random(20261004); B = 10,000; v sorted; LB = v[int(0.05*B)] = v[500]; alpha = 0.05 one-sided; p = (#{v <= 0} + 1) / (B + 1)

power_calculation.formula: clusters k = ((z_alpha + z_beta) * sigma_c / delta)^2 with sigma_c^2 = var_c(sum_c R - mean * n_c) / mbar^2; N_trades = k * mbar

assumptions.delta: +0.15 R per ticket after correct-side costs (same bar as H013/H015b)

power_calculation.design_effect: DEFF 1.384: rho(R) = 0.597 on 80 two-instrument clusters; mean cluster size 1.46
power_calculation.rho_use: rho is measured on the burned trades for variance (N, kill, futility simulation) only; it is never evidence
power_calculation.expected_duration: burned window: 254 eligible trades in ~272 trading days (~0.93 per trading day) -> N=747 is ~800 trading days (~3.2 years, ~late 2029/early 2030); trade rate unverified forward
power_calculation.joint_power_note: the six pass criteria are AND-ed and the kill and futility rules can stop a true edge, so the joint P(pass) is below the 0.80 single-test power; reported, not tuned. Simulation: clustered paths of the burned trades re-centred to mu, normal-approx cluster SE for the bounds, foil approximated as the burned pooled correct-side foil median (-0.0701) + 1.645*SD/sqrt(N) (research/evidence/quant/H016b_POWER_SIM_2026-10-04.py). Weakest criterion: both_instruments>0 (0.848 at +0.15)
power_calculation.normal_approx_check: CASSANDRA validated the normal-approx cluster SE against a percentile cluster bootstrap on the H016 sim (P(LB>0 | 0R) 0.047 vs 0.048; | +0.15 0.785 vs 0.785; P(futility | 0R) 0.162 vs 0.167; /workspace/h016_review/boot_vs_normal.out, not evidence)

binding_kill.rule: pooled cumulative R after correct-side costs <= -40R at any point from the first counted trade (canonical order: date, killzone, US100 before US500, entry time) -> FAILS (kill), stop counting
binding_kill.justification: clustered paths of the 254 filter-eligible burned trades re-centred (2,000 paths of 747 trades, seed 20261004, futility off): P(kill | +0.15R) = -30R 3.45%, -35R 1.85%, -40R 0.95%, -45R 0.60%, -50R 0.35%, -55R 0.10%, -60R 0.05%; -40R is the least negative level with P(kill | +0.15R) < 1%. With futility on (3,000 paths): (+0.15) 0.9%, (+0.10) 2.8%, (+0.00) 31.1%, (-0.10) 73.1%
binding_kill.kill_log: the first crossing of the kill line is logged ONCE with its row keys (sealed/KILL_LOG.json), never overwritten (CASSANDRA F5)

binding_futility.rule: fires ONCE, at exactly the 200th counted pooled trade (canonical order); never re-evaluated (no repeated peeking). Same session-cluster bootstrap on those 200 trades (clusters cut at trade 200 kept partial), seed 20261004, 10,000 resamples: upper one-sided 97.5% bound = v[int(0.975*10000) - 1] = v[9749]. If v[9749] < +0.10R -> FAILS (futility), stop counting
binding_futility.frozen_set: the first time counted N reaches 200, the 200 row keys, the bound and the decision are written ONCE to sealed/FUTILITY_SET.json (never overwritten, sealed until certification); futility is evaluated on exactly that set; a later backfill that reshuffles the canonical first 200 is reported, never used (CASSANDRA F5; = H015b v2 condition 4)
binding_futility.operating_characteristics: simulated (normal-approx cluster SE, 3,000 paths, K -40R): P(futility | +0.15) 0.9%, P(futility | +0.10) 2.9%, P(futility | +0.00) 8.2%, P(futility | -0.10) 14.7%

family_rule.clause: 'any later forward test added to the active family'
family_rule.applies: a PASSES (unadjusted) becomes MINT-clearable SURVIVES only if its primary one-sided p (statistical_test.p_value_for_family_rule, the session-cluster bootstrap) clears Holm across the active family of THREE tests H013, H014, H016b at one-sided alpha 0.05: thresholds 0.0167 / 0.025 / 0.05 (smallest p first, stop at the first failure). Otherwise 'PASSES (unadjusted), replication required'
family_rule.h015b: H015b is WITHDRAWN-PRE-DATA (ORION, 2026-10-04; research/summaries/2026-10-04_H015b_WITHDRAWAL.md; basis CASSANDRA ruling /home/box/hermes-x/reviews/post-wave1/CASSANDRA_H015B_WITHDRAWAL_RULING_2026-10-04.md): not FAILS, no verdict, not in the family. If its harness is ever run it is a non-binding diagnostic only (flat vs correct-side cost comparison), can never produce SURVIVES, FAILS or a board entry, and its R stays sealed until H016b reaches a verdict (pass, fail, kill or futility), because its tickets overlap H016b's

orion_ruling_a.text: ACKNOWLEDGED: unfinished, killed or futile tests enter Holm at p=1; Holm is re-run each time a test completes; a SURVIVES once granted is never revoked (it already cleared the strictest threshold, 0.0125, and later re-runs only loosen thresholds).
orion_ruling_a.implementation: at any decision time, every unfinished family test enters Holm with p = 1 and a killed or futile test has p = 1; Holm is re-run when each test completes

orion_ruling_b.scope: H015b vs H016b (FTN-REV variants); retained as the standing rule although H015b is withdrawn
text: 1. Each is judged only on its own binding criteria plus Holm, and their trades are never pooled.
2. If exactly one passes, its SURVIVES is variant-specific (the stop/pip fix matters), with the failing variant's result disclosed beside it.
3. If both pass, it is ONE finding for the family rule, not replication; a fresh forward test under a new ID is required before MINT clearance beyond the paper limits.
4. If they point in opposite directions (one killed, the other passes), the passing one needs CASSANDRA's written check that the difference is explained by the fix and not noise before SURVIVES.
(b)2: a variant-specific SURVIVES for a flat-cost variant needs its correct-side co-report to pass as well.
(b)4: CASSANDRA's written check needs the fill-fragility co-report (H016b amendment 6) to be non-flipping.

family_rule.not_independent: H015b and H016b are REV variants on the same instruments and sessions, so a pass in one is NOT independent replication of the other
family_rule.never_relaxed: kills and the binding futility rule are per-test and are never relaxed by the family rule
family_rule.why: three tests at alpha 0.05: ~14% chance that at least one passes by luck with no edge if independent
family_rule.co_report: ORION's non-binding Holm co-report across H013 / H014 / H016b is kept in every report
